The issue was that `dict.update()` replaces nested dicts entirely instead of merging them. The fix recursively merges nested dicts key-by-key: when both the override value and the existing value are dicts, it calls `merge()` recursively on them. It also handles the None case (unsetting keys) as documented. All tests pass.
